title: GraphQuon 2024: the workshop and its website

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a rehearsal room for the biggest computer graphics conference in the world, where nobody is afraid of tough questions. That's GraphQuon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. It's the annual Quebec and Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop for East-Canadian graphics labs. Students present work in progress to a friendly but constructively critical audience, and get feedback before the real submission deadlines.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: At ÉTS in Montréal, on November ninth and tenth. Labs across both provinces take turns hosting, and 2024 was ÉTS's turn. Antoine helped build and host the website on GitHub Pages, so schedules, registration and past editions all lived in one place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So he was on the organizing side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, the web side. He learned the critical path: bios on time, PDF links that work, and a schedule page that reads well on a phone in a hallway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Students from McGill, Université de Montréal, Sherbrooke, Toronto, Waterloo and more. Clara Kim from Waterloo won best presentation, and several others earned honourable mentions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine talked with Masha Shugrina from NVIDIA. One demo was Diffusion Texture Painting, from SIGGRAPH 2024: you paint on a three-D mesh with a diffusion brush, so strokes stay seamless and you can blend complex reference textures interactively. Think of it as a brush that understands the surface.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Gaussian splat style scan of a scene you could walk around in, which makes spatial content feel immediate without a heavy offline pipeline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In 2025 Antoine presented at the Toronto edition. Organizing first made presenting calmer, since he already knew where everything was. The full write-up has the schedule and the photos.
